name: Sequins
tagline: Stripe's read-only key-value server for Hadoop batch output, loaded from HDFS or S3; archived in 2023.
description: Sequins was a Go service from Stripe for serving the output of batch jobs with low latency. You point it at a source root on local disk, HDFS or S3 containing databases and versions of Hadoop SequenceFiles (from MapReduce, Spark or Impala); each node mirrors and indexes its partitions into local Sparkey hash files and answers HTTP GET requests by key, with no client library and no runtime dependency on Hadoop. Updates are whole new versions that nodes switch to atomically, and a ZooKeeper-coordinated cluster partitions and replicates data so it keeps serving through node failures. It filled the niche Voldemort's read-only stores once did. Stripe stopped maintaining it and archived the repository in July 2023.
statusNote: Stripe archived the repository in July 2023 and marked it inactive. Consider serving batch output from RocksDB-, ScyllaDB- or DynamoDB-backed stores.

scale.notes: Partitions and replicates read-only datasets across a ZooKeeper-coordinated cluster; local data is only a cache of the source root.

strengths: Serves Hadoop/Spark batch output directly with millisecond key lookups
Atomic version switching: publish a new dataset by writing a new directory
No runtime dependency on HDFS once data is mirrored
Plain HTTP interface with no client library
weaknesses: Read-only: no individual writes, only whole-dataset versions
useCases: Serving precomputed features or scores from batch pipelines
Low-latency lookups over nightly Hadoop job output
Reference design for versioned read-only key-value serving
notIdealFor: Workloads with individual writes or updates
